title: Repeat Emergency Supplies of One Drug — Adjustment to Supply Days
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit — clinical pharmacy edit note.** When a drug turned away at the counter for prior authorization has already received emergency supplies, the emergency supply days are adjusted.

**Rule.** The repeat-supply adjustment looks at emergency supplies of the same drug dispensed in the last three months: minus five days for two or more, minus three days for exactly one, and nothing for none.

The adjustment is added to the request days in forming the counted emergency supply days, and the one-day floor applies to those counted days as a whole, after every addition to them. The drug is the one named on the latest counter rejection for prior authorization on the member's pharmacy coverage; the supplies counted are the emergency supply dispensings of that drug on the member's pharmacy claims with a fill date in the last three months.

### Adjustment table

| Emergency supplies of the same drug, last three months | Repeat-supply adjustment |
|---|---|
| Two or more | Minus 5 days (a signed adjustment of -5) |
| Exactly one | Minus 3 days (a signed adjustment of -3) |
| None | Nothing |

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

| Request days | Earlier emergency supplies of the drug | Adjustment | Request days with the adjustment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | 1 | Minus 3 | 6 |
| 5 | 2 | Minus 5 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 | Minus 5 | minus 2 |
| 9 | 0 | Nothing | 9 |

The last column is not yet floored: the one-day floor is applied to the counted emergency supply days as a whole, once every addition to them has been made.
